atoms.b:
Martin Luther King Jr. (1929-1968)
Born “Michael King”, January 15, 1929 in Atlanta, Georgia, Martin Luther King attended segregated public schools in Georgia. He graduated from college in 1948. Martin became a national leader in the ((Civil_Rights)) Movement of the 1950s and 60s. The goal of the Movement was to achieve equal rights for African Americans.

Martin L.K. helped organise both the Montgomery ((Bus_Boycott)) in 1955 and the March on Washington in 1963, where he gave his ((famous_speech)) “I Have a Dream”. There, he described his vision of a racially equal America. The March was one of the largest marches in American history, with more than 250,000 people of all colours.

In between those events, Martin L.K. visited India to study ((non-violent)) tactics, employed by Mahatma Gandhi. He further contributed to the ((achievement)) of the Civil Rights Act, which was signed in 1964. In the same year, he was the youngest person ever, at age 35, to receive the Nobel Peace Prize for non-violent resistance.

He was assassinated on April 4, 1968 in Memphis, Tennessee, while supporting a workers' strike. After his death, he was awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 1977. In 2011, a ((memorial)) was built to remember Martin Luther King Jr. This is the first memorial in the National Mall to honour an African-American ((individual)).

instruction.text: Read the text and choose all correct statements.

atoms.text: Martin Luther King Jr.'s philosophy of non-violence advanced the goal of universal freedom and equality. He remained true to his principles and never gave up the fight for equality. A lot of things have changed for African Americans but systemic racism and injustice still exists. Today, the Black Lives Matter campaign calls for racial equality and social change. That is why Black Lives Matter is frequently seen as a renewed form of the Civil Rights Movement. Also, both have used non-violent protest as a political tool. But the two movements differ in important ways. For example, Black Lives Matter does not have one central leader comparable to Martin Luther King Jr.
